players.product: system-level test (SLT) platforms for AI accelerators and power test equipment

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Lawrence Wu: Q2 2026 consolidated revenue reached TWD 13.53 billion, up 110% year on year and another record, with net income of TWD 5.12 billion (+162%) and EPS of TWD 12.15; gross margin slipped to 61% from 63% in Q1 mainly on short-term higher costs of DRAM, passive components and ICs, and Chroma may adjust prices by product, very likely this year, with new products reflecting the component costs. Non-operating income of TWD 1.27 billion came from disposing of ADLINK shares and employee housing assets; cash and short-term investments were TWD 13.68 billion, inventory turnover days improved from 224 to 177, H1 free cash flow was TWD 3.29 billion, and capex should moderate now that major construction of the second manufacturing facility is complete. Chroma's Jennifer Chien (call host): test instruments and ATS revenue rose 14% quarter on quarter and 129% year on year, mainly on AI server power applications, which account for over 60% of this power business, and the segment's H1 sales already exceed its total 2025 revenue; the semiconductor segment had Q2 revenue of TWD 4.4 billion, up 29% quarter on quarter and double year on year, led by system-level testers and photonics.

Chroma's Jennifer Chien (call host): AI power-test customers 'already block off the whole year' with orders they have not adjusted, and keep pushing Chroma to speed up delivery; testers for 400 V and 800 V HVDC have shipped in volume from day one, with monthly shipments about the same. ESS battery-test demand keeps increasing and orders are 'piling up', more than guided at the start of the year, with the battery project shipping from Q3. Legacy final-test demand, guided flat for 2026, rose from Q2 as newcomers taking over legacy parts buy new tools, and may grow maybe 10% or 20% this year.
quarterly_data.figure: legacy final-test demand maybe +10% or 20% in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Chroma's Jennifer Chien (call host): the capacity constraint that limited power-tester deliveries last year eased once Chroma's phase II facility was ready at the beginning of this year and started ramping.

Chroma's Jennifer Chien (call host): Chroma has POs for CPO Insertion 3 and Insertion 4O testing that start contributing in H2 2026, and order sizes are bigger than three months ago as CPO's test complexity raises units; customers have so far ordered only up to Insertion 4O. Insertion 4 was '100% initiated by Chroma', with no competitor, while Insertion 3 has existing peers; the testers are 100% Chroma's own technology. Current CPO customers are NVIDIA ('NV') and Marvell, which is not yet ramped. Semiconductor and photonics test will be the main contributors in H2, which Chroma expects to outperform H1, driven by SLT for AI / HPC / ASIC and photonics for optical communication and CPO.

Chroma's Jennifer Chien (call host): for AMD's high-power-density chiplet accelerator (named MI300 on the call) SLT test time runs six to eight hours against the customer's four-hour target, and the customer recently revised its order units up by about 70%, almost double, for delivery from Q3. Chroma also tests CPUs, including Google's CPU, with CPU demand still rising, a new business for the next 12 months. On its final-test handler for AI chips she said it is doing well, 'the first time we don't need to do debug', and the next customer will adopt it; meaningful revenue should come from this year and a large ramp maybe next year.
quarterly_data.figure: SLT order units revised up about 70%; test time six to eight hours
